title: GST State Code List 2026 (State-Wise GST Codes & Jurisdiction Details)
summary: Find GST state codes and jurisdiction details for 2026. Ensure correct GST registration and filing compliance for businesses, service providers, and freelancers.

Toggle


### Key Takeaways


- The first two digits of a GSTIN identify the state or Union Territory in which the taxpayer is registered.
- Frequently searched codes include 06 for Haryana, 07 for Delhi, 09 for Uttar Pradesh, 27 for Maharashtra, 29 for Karnataka and 36 for Telangana.
- Code 37 belongs to Andhra Pradesh and code 38 belongs to Ladakh. They are not GST commissionerate codes.
- A state code helps identify the registration location, but the supplier’s location and place of supply determine whether CGST and SGST or IGST applies.
- GST registrations are state-specific. Moving a business to another state generally requires a fresh registration in the new state.


GST state codes are two-digit numeric codes assigned to states and Union Territories in India. These codes form the first two digits of every GSTIN. In a vast country like India, each registration location needs a unique identifier under the GST framework to support tax administration and business compliance across the country.


This guide covers the complete GST state code list for 2026, what each code means, how to use it correctly and what can happen when a code is entered incorrectly.


##


**What are GST State Codes?**


The first two digits of any 15-digit[GSTIN](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/what-is-goods-and-service-tax-identification-number/) are called the GST state code. They identify the state or Union Territory in which a business is registered.


Before[Goods and Services Tax](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/what-is-gst-goods-and-service-tax/) was introduced, indirect tax rules varied across states. GST state codes provide a standard way to identify the registration location, allocate revenue and distinguish GSTINs issued in different states.


State codes appear on GST invoices, returns, e-way bills and verification records. Although they may look like a small detail, an incorrect code can create mismatches across invoices and filings.


#### **How to Read a GST State Code in a GSTIN**


When identifying a GSTIN, the first two digits represent the state where the business has been registered. For example, the GST state code “06” represents Haryana (HR) and the GST state code “29” represents Karnataka (KA).


For example: 36SBAKR3146E1Z2. Code 36 represents Telangana, therefore, this business has been registered in Telangana. If you receive an invoice from a Hyderabad-based vendor with a GSTIN starting with 29, you must verify it prior to processing the invoice. Similarly, Cashfree’s GSTIN starts with 29, which indicates our business is registered in Karnataka.

##


Why Is the GST State Code Important?


The two-digit GST state code identifies where a taxpayer is registered. It supports revenue allocation, tax reporting and verification under India’s GST system.


- **Intra-state and inter-state tax:** The code helps establish the registration location. However, the applicable tax is ultimately based on the supplier’s location and the place of supply. Intra-state supplies generally attract[CGST](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/what-is-cgst-central-goods-and-services-tax/) and SGST, while inter-state supplies generally attract[IGST](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/what-is-igst/) .
- **Unique identification:** The first two digits help distinguish registrations issued under the same PAN in different states.
- **Fewer return errors:** Correct state-code mapping reduces mismatches while[filing GST returns](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/gst-return-filing/) .
- **Revenue allocation:** State codes help the GST system allocate tax revenue to the appropriate jurisdiction.
- **Vendor verification:** Businesses can associate a GSTIN with its registered state before onboarding a supplier or processing an invoice.


##


**Why are GST Codes Needed?**


GST state codes are used across several business and compliance workflows:


- **GSTIN generation:** The code forms the first two digits of the 15-character GSTIN.
- **Invoice issuance:** The supplier’s and recipient’s GSTINs must be recorded accurately on applicable tax invoices.
- **Tax determination:** The registration location is one input used with place-of-supply rules to determine the applicable GST treatment.
- **GST return filing:** Correct GSTINs help businesses report purchases and sales against the right counterparty and jurisdiction.
- **E-way bills:** State codes appear in[e-way bill records](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/eway-bill-online-generation/) for applicable movement of goods, including qualifying intra-state and inter-state movement.
- **Product and service classification:** State codes are separate from[HSN and SAC codes](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/hsn-sac-code-gst/) , which classify the goods or services supplied.
- **Audit and compliance checks:** Correct codes support assessments, invoice matching and[input tax credit](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/input-tax-credit-gst/) reviews.


***Also read:[GST Registration Online Process, Documents and Fees](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/gst-registration-online-process-documents/)***


##


**How to Find Your GST Jurisdiction?**


Your GST jurisdiction is your tax authority and is based on your state code and your GSTN registration information.


You can find your GST jurisdiction by following the steps given below:


1. Visit the GST portal (gst.gov.in).
2. Click on the Search Taxpayer tab.
3. Enter your GSTIN.
4. Review your jurisdiction details, it will show you your centre and state jurisdiction.


Cashfree provides a[GST verification tool](https://www.cashfree.com/gst-verification/) that allows businesses to verify their GST jurisdiction along with their GSTIN records in one step.


##


Central vs State GST Jurisdiction


When you search for your jurisdiction, you will find two options listed: state jurisdiction option and center jurisdiction. State jurisdiction implies that a state gst officer is responsible for administering your registration and responding to audit notices, assessment notices etc. Center jurisdiction implies that a Central GST (CBIC) officer is responsible for doing the same.


The difference ultimately depends upon the nature of the business and its turnover. Generally, most small and medium-sized businesses are categorized as being under state jurisdiction. Large businesses and/or certain industry-specific businesses may fall under central jurisdiction. It is important to know the right jurisdiction so that you can accurately respond to any noticed sent by the GST authorities.


##


**Consequences of Using the Wrong GST State Code**


An incorrect state code is not always a minor oversight. It can cause GST return mismatches, invoice rejection, delayed input tax credit and follow-up from tax authorities.


- **Invoice and return mismatches:** If a GSTIN is entered incorrectly, the recipient may not find the invoice against the expected registration in its records.
- **Incorrect tax treatment:** A wrong GSTIN can contribute to incorrect CGST, SGST or IGST treatment, although place-of-supply rules must also be considered.
- **E-invoice rejection:** The Invoice Registration Portal may reject an e-invoice when the GSTIN or state information is inconsistent. For taxpayers covered by mandatory e-invoicing, a valid Invoice Reference Number is required for the document to qualify as a valid e-invoice.
- **Vendor-onboarding risk:** An incorrect or inactive GSTIN can create compliance and payment delays. If a business uses a PAN across multiple registrations, a[GST search by PAN](https://www.cashfree.com/gst-search-by-pan/) can help identify the associated GSTINs before selecting the correct one.


Businesses should review supplier master data, validate GSTINs at onboarding and periodically recheck registration status. Developers can also test a GSTIN verification flow in[Cashfree Dev Studio](https://www.cashfree.com/devstudio/secureid) before implementing it.


##


**Can You Change a GST State Code After Relocating?**


Not within the same GST registration. GST registrations are state-specific. If a business relocates from one state to another, it generally needs to cancel the existing registration as applicable and apply for a fresh GST registration in the new state. The GST portal’s official registration guidance confirms that an interstate relocation cannot be completed by amending the state in the existing registration.


##


Conclusion


GST state codes make it possible to identify the registration location from the first two digits of a GSTIN. The most important practical step is to verify the complete GSTIN instead of relying on the state code alone. This helps businesses avoid invoice mismatches, incorrect vendor records and preventable compliance delays.

**FAQs**


**What is GST State Code?**


GST State Code is a two-digit number assigned to each state under GST. It forms the first two digits of a GSTIN and identifies the state of registration.


**How many GST state codes are there in India?**


There are 38 GST state codes, covering all Indian states and union territories.


**Why are there separate state codes for GST?**


State codes ensure that the tax revenue is attributed and distributed accurately, reflecting the destination-based nature of GST.


**How often are state codes updated?**


While the foundational structure remains consistent, geopolitical events or administrative decisions can lead to periodic updates.


**What’s the distinction between CGST, SGST, and IGST?** Both CGST (Central Goods and Services Tax) and SGST (State Goods and Services Tax) apply to transactions within a state, whereas IGST (Integrated Goods and Services Tax) is designed for transactions that span across different states. Learn detailed differences here.


**Can I change my state code if I relocate my business?** Yes, but it requires a thorough process of updating your GST registration and ensuring compliance with the new state’s regulations.


**What happens if I use the wrong state code in my GST returns?** It can lead to mismatches, potential penalties, and legal implications.
